doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

chapter: Jazz's place and the band's future
title: Why jazz is undervalued and the college circuit
summary: Vollmer sees jazz as black, syncopated and not classical, discusses conservatory training, and wishes for college bookings presenting jazz history.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: A good friend of mine from high school that I — he was the other jazz guy in the high school and we kept up for a long time, he felt like, you know Ben Webster should have been given a stipend of $10,000 a year in order to stay in the country so he didn’t have to live in Denmark.
Why is it? Why is jazz not —

I think first of all it’s primarily black music. Secondly it’s syncopated, it’s not classical, and you know there’s prejudice against anything that’s not classical primarily, there’s the snootiness to it, and you know unfortunately some of that has rubbed off even on the jazz musicians, who feel they’ve got to go to Juilliard. But of course it’s changed. At one time it was very emotional and you didn’t have to go to school, you had to feel it. But now maybe in order to come up with a different way of playing or approaching it another way or, I don’t say to advance it, but to change it, maybe you have to come at it from a different perspective. I’m still stuck in the older way.
But somebody like Phil Schaap, he does the whole spectrum. I mean, you know, I prefer Hodges to Parker, which is a heresy.

Yeah. I’m with you because well my favorite people are not usually the real innovators. It’s the people that may take from them. At any rate, jazz is now a highly respected art form but it’s not any easier to make a living at it unless you go through academia.
Right. No I wish I had succeeded a little bit more to get on the college circuit and to present that — what I’m really presenting in a way is the history of jazz music.
